criteria.rationale: Examined L1 and L2. L2 is verified: both plan digests include accepted_limits (digest tests pass). L1 is an accepted risk mitigated by the brief listing the limits as data and allowing a dispute; a dispute blocks or not according to its disposition, as any finding. Neither covers the parser dropping text (N1).
The change adds pure parsing and bounded file reads with no shared state or new lifecycle.
New fields are omitted when empty, schemas allow additional properties, and earlier templates keep their digests.
Plan, bundle, brief, conclusion and governance outcomes consume the new fields consistently.
Unsealed limits, blank reasons, nested lists and unreadable ADRs return specific messages; silent parser cases are in N1 and N2.

Checked omitempty on plan, bundle, draft and attestation fields and the test that a plan without limits keeps the earlier bundle plan digest; only the unpublished review-brief/11 digest was re-recorded.

D1 and D2 address the cause: a sealed declaration lets a finding be classified within-limit instead of reopening rounds, read from the bundle and not the current spec. The design assessment lists no structural deltas, so no mappings are owed.
The changed paths match the spec artifacts and artifact-check strict exits 0; no round cap or other non-goal was added.

within-limit requires an id sealed in the bundle and a non-blank reason; manual attest cannot name a limit and so is refused; ADRs are read as regular bounded files. The truncated-limit defect that widens a limit is filed as N1.

A section, two sealed fields, one disposition and a ready check are close to the smallest sufficient design; the hand-written Markdown reader is the costly part and would justify a stricter one-line-or-refuse format if it keeps producing defects.

findings.action: A limit is still sealed cut short with no problem reported. (a) A wrapped line without indentation is part of the Markdown list item (lazy continuation), but it falls to the default case and ends the entry: '- L1: An escape is open. Accepted because a shim covers it' followed by 'only on Linux and only for children.' seals only the first line, confirmed through ParseAcceptedLimits and Store.ReviewPlan with a test overlay. (b) An indented fenced block inside an item closes it (line 74-84), so the indented 'and only on Linux.' after it is dropped. The lost qualifier broadens the limit in the plan, digests and brief, where the reviewer cannot see it. Round 10 reintroduced (a), which round 9 read into the entry. It is not covered by L1, which concerns what the implementer writes, not text the engine drops. Read the whole item, or report it and do not seal it, with tests for both.
Report limit-like lines in the section that are not read, or read lists and headings indented up to three spaces, with tests.
findings.rationale: Valid Markdown is ignored with no problem and a passing lint: a list indented by one to three spaces ('  - L1: ...'), an indented '### Accepted limits' heading (line 88), and '+' or ordered items all yield zero limits; a sibling indented by one space is reported as a nested list and refuses L1. Nothing is accepted wrongly, but the author is not told the declaration was not read. The indented list and heading were read before round 10.
